long_biography.plain_text:
Peter Sperling's support for coastal conservation helped a community campaign reach a crucial fundraising deadline. In 2003, he and his wife, Stephanie, pledged five million dollars to protect Ellwood Mesa near Santa Barbara. Its coastal bluffs and monarch butterfly habitat were threatened by residential development.

The gift secured the campaign's immediate target and recognised years of local volunteer work. It followed their support for preserving Arroyo Hondo and adding land to El Capitan Beach State Park. The Ellwood project combined public and private funding with a municipal land exchange, securing open space that would pass to the City of Goleta.
